title: Ireland's Split Economy Sets Stage for Bruising Budget Battle This Autumn · 14 Sep
keywords: Ireland economy, Irish budget 2026, GDP growth, modified domestic demand, Irish inflation, HICP, CSO, cost of living, fiscal policy, multinational corporations, domestic demand, tax receipts, Irish politics, public spending, housing Ireland
notes: Ireland's headline GDP surged 10.2% in the second quarter of 2026, but the domestic economy quietly contracted, exposing a growing gap between national statistics and the daily reality faced by households and workers. With tax receipts running well ahead of expectations, the government holds real fiscal firepower heading into the autumn budget. The political fight over how to spend it is already shaping up to be one of the most contentious in years.
